title: Cerebellum Atlas
subtitle: Map lobules, peduncles, deep nuclei and cerebellar loops
altText: Interactive chalkboard-style anatomical atlas of Cerebellum with labelled regions and pathway relationships.
learningObjectives: Identify the cerebellar hemispheres, vermis, lobes, peduncles and deep nuclei.
Trace major input and output routes through cerebellar peduncles.
Explain motor and cognitive-affective consequences of cerebellar disruption.

sections.explainSimply: The cerebellum fine-tunes movement, timing and prediction. It also contributes to language, attention and emotional regulation through loops with the cortex.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Cerebellar function is best understood as error-based calibration across motor and cognitive systems, not merely balance and coordination.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Cerebellar cortex receives mossy- and climbing-fibre input, transforms signals through granule and Purkinje-cell circuitry, and modulates output through deep nuclei. Cerebello-thalamo-cortical loops support timing, prediction, adaptation and optimisation across motor and nonmotor domains.
sections.thinkOfItLike: It is the brain’s quality-control studio: it compares the intended performance with the actual performance and adjusts the next attempt.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Cerebellar lesions may produce cognitive-affective changes, slowed processing, dysprosody or executive inefficiency in addition to ataxia.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Assuming a normal strength examination excludes meaningful cerebellar dysfunction misses timing, coordination and cognitive-affective effects.
sections.clinicalPearl: The cerebellum does not initiate most behaviour; it calibrates the precision, timing and adaptability of behaviour.
sections.practicalExample: A posterior cerebellar lesion may leave basic strength intact yet produce dysmetria, slowed set-shifting and flattened affect.
sections.limitationsCautions: Cerebellar cognitive-affective findings are variable and should be corroborated with neurological signs, imaging and functional change.

anatomy.label: Vermis
anatomy.function: Midline posture, gait and axial coordination
anatomy.connections: Vestibular, spinal and cortical information; projects via Fastigial and vestibular pathways.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Assess vermis in the context of lesion location, laterality, tract involvement and functional change.

anatomy.label: Lateral hemispheres
anatomy.outputs: Dentate nucleus to thalamus and cortex
anatomy.connections: Pontocerebellar input from association cortex; projects via Dentate nucleus to thalamus and cortex.
anatomy.associatedDisorders: Limb dysmetria, executive and language changes
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Assess lateral hemispheres in the context of lesion location, laterality, tract involvement and functional change.

anatomy.label: Flocculonodular lobe
anatomy.connections: Vestibular input; projects via Vestibular nuclei.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Assess flocculonodular lobe in the context of lesion location, laterality, tract involvement and functional change.

anatomy.label: Deep nuclei
anatomy.function: Primary output hubs of the cerebellum
anatomy.inputs: Purkinje-cell inhibition and collateral excitatory input
anatomy.connections: Purkinje-cell inhibition and collateral excitatory input; projects via Thalamic, red-nucleus and vestibular targets.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Assess deep nuclei in the context of lesion location, laterality, tract involvement and functional change.

anatomy.label: Cerebellar peduncles
anatomy.function: White-matter gateways connecting cerebellum with brainstem
anatomy.inputs: Spinal, vestibular, olivary and pontine pathways
anatomy.connections: Spinal, vestibular, olivary and pontine pathways; projects via Brainstem, thalamic and cortical loops.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Assess cerebellar peduncles in the context of lesion location, laterality, tract involvement and functional change.
